_comment: How Tools/Blender/build_ai_ship.py turns the Meshy 'Ironclad Starfighter' export into Vanguard_Meshy.blend. Coordinates are Blender metres after orienting and scaling: +X nose, +Y the ship's left, +Z up. Measured on the oriented model (18. 9. 2026): 14.0 x 11.44 x 6.18 m, one connected surface; four engine nacelles (centres y +-4.3, z +1.8 / -1.1), nozzles recessed at x -5.8 .. -6.7; skids fused into the hull: one nose skid on the centreline (x 1.7 .. 3.6, 1.1 m under the belly at -2.0) and two main skids at y +-2.0 .. 2.75 (x -4.6 .. -2.6, 0.55 m under the belly at -2.56); cabin x 2 .. 4.5, roof 1.6 .. 2.1 m.

Gear._comment: Everything wholly below the belly at the skids. The stubs between belly and cut stay on the hull as mounts.

decimate._comment: Importance 1 = keep detail, 0 = decimate freely; the last matching rule wins. protect_factor scales how much importance matters.

importance._what: upward faces (seen from the chase camera)
inside the nozzles and the rear bulkhead

rebake._comment: New UV atlas on the decimated meshes and the full-resolution model baked onto it (Cycles, selected to active). Meshy's own atlas has thousands of tiny islands that decimation welds together, and its normal map is almost flat: the detail is geometry.

emissive._comment: Nozzle discs get the M_Ship_<Ship>_Emissive slot, which the game makes glow with engine load.

collision.name: canopy (own hull: remove it for a modelled cockpit interior)

Cockpit._comment: the pilot's eye, 14 cm above the front edge of the cabin roof: without a modelled interior everything is culled from inside (cockpit_view_survey.py). The nose falls away at 29 degrees, more than the view's 25 degrees down, so it shows only with free look.

Exit._comment: beside the cabin on the right (Blender -Y), on the ground
